elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed..." — "each Party" makes the cap mutual, and no retained sentence states Customer's liability is unlimited.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: "the greater of (i) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and (ii) USD 1,000,000" — correct basis (fees paid or payable, not broader "all amounts"), correct temporal anchor (preceding the claim) and the USD 1,000,000 floor.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained 7(a): "NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE FOR ANY CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, INDIRECT, PUNITIVE, SPECIAL OR OTHER SIMILAR DAMAGES" — mutual by its terms; left untouched.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "'Excluded Claims' means a Party's breach of its confidentiality... obligations", and the cap applies "Except for Excluded Claims".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims expressly includes "breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations".
Excluded Claims includes "its indemnification obligations"; also consistent with retained 7(a) which carves indemnification out of the consequential-damages exclusion.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims includes "its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights".

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: "Customer's payment obligations under this Agreement shall not be considered damages subject to this cap." — covers payment obligations generally, not a narrow Fees subset.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "each Party's total aggregate liability... shall not exceed" — bilateral.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Cap floor is the "fees paid or payable by Customer... in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim", with a USD 1,000,000 alternative under a greater-of formula.
"Except for Excluded Claims"; Excluded Claims includes "its indemnification obligations".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims includes "breach of its confidentiality... obligations".

reasons: The finding of deviation is correct: the original Section 7 contained only a mutual consequential-damages exclusion and no aggregate cap anywhere in the cited operative text, so the fallback element 'cap based on 12 months of fees' failed outright.

The inserted language completes every preferred element in one concise addition: a mutual greater-of cap with the exact fees paid-or-payable basis, the 12-month pre-claim lookback, the USD 1,000,000 floor, the full Excluded Claims list (confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, other party's IP infringement), and the Customer-payment-obligations carve-out.

Minimality holds: the existing 7(a) mutual exclusion (including its favourable indemnification/confidentiality carve-outs from that exclusion) is retained verbatim with no deletions or paraphrase, and no extras (survival tails, procedures, added damages categories, explanatory examples) were introduced. The payment-obligation sentence is required by a selected element, so it is not an extra.

Intent is preserved: the carve-outs in retained 7(a) and the new Excluded Claims definition are consistent rather than contradictory, no defined term is left dangling ('Excluded Claims' is defined in the same inserted text), and the revenue-share fee mechanics in Section 5 are unaffected — the USD 1,000,000 floor simply prevents an illusory fees-only cap.

No repair needed. Optional polish only (not a defect): the model language anchors the lookback to 'the event giving rise to the claim' rather than 'the claim'; the rendered wording tracks the checklist element literally and is acceptable.
